reasoning_traces.think:
EventNet operates in two stages: first, 2D keypoints from players, ball, and table are encoded into CLS tokens via a Keypoints Transformer. These tokens form a temporal sequence Z ∈ ℝ^{T×D}. Then, a Time-to-Event Transformer processes Z to produce time-to-event vectors T ∈ ℝ^{T×2}, encoding proximity to previous and next events. The event detection logic identifies E_t as the frame minimizing sum of absolute time-to-event indicators. This dual-time encoding enables robust temporal localization without requiring prior event annotations. Failure modes include occlusion, poor keypoint detection, or insufficient temporal context beyond model receptive field. The system leverages viewpoint augmentation and 3D reprojection to enhance generalization across diverse video conditions.
